title: Qualcomm's Downside if Chip Prices Continue to Fall
text: Qualcomm ( QCOM ) chipsets pricing will likely decline around 10% in 2010 from around $18.10 in 2009 to $16.30 in 2010, based on our estimates. We believe that the factors leading to lower chipsets prices are: 1) rising competition from players like Broadcom ( BRCM ), Texas Instruments ( TXN ) and Infineon Wireless, which was acquired by Intel ( INTC ), and 2) new chips designed for lower price points to tap emerging markets demand. Hence the fast Snapdragon growth should slow down the average chipsets pricing decline.

title: Nvidia's Mobile & Gaming Chips Could Lift Outlook
text: Nvidia competes with Qualcomm ( QCOM ), Texas Instruments ( TXN ), Infineon, and Broadcom ( BRCM ) in the mobile computing processor market. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) revenues from mobile computing chips like Tegra and GoForce have started to rise, and we expect this trend to continue at a faster pace led by growing adoption of smartphones, PDAs, portable media players, gaming consoles and tablet PCs. Apart from smartphones, Nvidia's Tegra chips are present in Microsoft's Zune portable media player as well as Sony's PlayStation gaming console.

title: Growing Atom Share Adds Little Value to Intel Stock
text: Intel's Atom competes with AMD's ( AMD ) Athlon Neo, Qualcomm's ( QCOM ) Snapdragon, and Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Tegra microprocessors. Further ahead, we expect Atom's market share to grow as it enters the smartphone and tablet form factors.
